claim: Random 3-SAT cost peaks where about half of formulas are satisfiable (clause/variable ratio near 4.3 at 50-140 variables) and is easy on both sides; the transition is sharp, and first-order (discontinuous) for 3-SAT. The exact 3-SAT threshold is known only from experiment and physics estimates; the proof is for large k.
agent_test: Generate test problems at, below and above the threshold; check that gains from a solver tool differ by hardness band, at equal tokens.

claim: Chaff-style engineering (two watched literals, VSIDS, restarts with learned clauses) made industrial SAT practical: 1 to 2 orders of magnitude faster than SATO/GRASP on the authors' own hard EDA sets.
agent_test: Not an agent test. Measure solver wall-time against LLM tokens on 20 mid-size instances to confirm a solver call is cheap.

claim: Having the LLM write a declarative constraint spec and letting an SMT/SAT solver find the answer beats imperative program-of-thought and CoT on constraint-heavy tasks, and is on par on plain arithmetic (SatLM GSM 71.8 vs ProgLM 72.7).
agent_test: Same model, same token budget: (a) CoT, (b) write Python, (c) write Z3 spec and run. Compare on 100 constraint puzzles and 100 plain word problems.

claim: The solver call is the active ingredient. SatLM with the spec but no solver (answer from the model) gets GSM-Sys 26.6 vs standard 21.0 and SatLM 69.4; a CoT solver on the spec gets 54.5 (+8 over CoT). LINC's Scratchpad (same formulas, model's own verdict) also gives no gain.
agent_test: Ablate the tool call: let the agent write the spec but answer from its own head. Expect little gain over plain.

claim: Translation is the bottleneck, not solving: GPT-4 executable rate 79.9% FOLIO and 32.6% AR-LSAT (about 100% on synthetic sets); 13-38% syntax errors in LINC; GPT-4 NL-to-FOL execution accuracy 63.8 on FOLIO.
agent_test: Log the share of specs that parse and run, and accuracy conditional on running, per task type.

claim: Whether solver pipelines beat CoT with a strong model on real-language logic is contested: Logic-LM reports GPT-4 FOLIO 78.92 vs CoT 70.58, while LINC reports GPT-4 LINC 72.5 vs CoT 75.3 (McNemar p=0.58). Gains are large on synthetic ProofWriter (LINC 98.3, SatLM depth 5 99.7) and shrink on human-written sets.
agent_test: Run both arms on one fixed human-written set with identical prompts; use a paired McNemar test, not raw accuracy gaps.

claim: Solver-error self-refinement mainly raises the share of formulas that execute, not correctness: Logic-LM average executable gain 5.01 points, FOLIO accuracy +0.5; Logic-LM++ pairwise-compare backtracking adds about 6 points (GPT-4) and 3 (GPT-3.5), nothing on ProofWriter, and slightly hurts GPT-3.5 on FOLIO (62.80 to 62.25 as reported).
agent_test: Compare naive retry on error with retry plus a keep-the-better-version check, at equal tokens.

claim: Distinct solver outputs (UNSAT, ambiguous, error) are usable signals: abstaining on them lifts SatLM selective accuracy (GSM-Sys 77.1 vs 45.2 for ProgLM, coverage 90.0 vs 95.8), and Z3 unsat cores can be turned into repair advice (Hao: 78.6% repaired, 81.6% with 20 iterations, on only 12 modified queries).
agent_test: Route on solver result type: UNSAT to revise spec, multiple models to add constraints, error to reformat. Compare with one fixed retry policy.

claim: Text-only LLMs are weak at search-style reasoning and especially at proving unsatisfiability: SATBench hard UNSAT mean 39.3% vs hard SAT 66.7% (chance 50); ZebraLogic grid accuracy falls to near 0 on x-large grids for non-reasoning models.
agent_test: Give the agent hard UNSAT instances; measure SAT-bias rate with and without a solver tool.

claim: Scale alone does not fix hard instances; only models with long hidden reasoning break the plateau, and they still degrade: SATBench hard accuracy plateaus near 50-53% across families; ZebraLogic x-large o1 42.5, R1 28.5, o1-preview 17.0, GPT-4o 0.5.
agent_test: Not scale-testable by us. Test instead that tool use closes the gap on x-large puzzles for a mid-size model.
note_gap_search: MathConstraint 2026 (d01) shows current reasoning models (GPT-5.5 at max effort 66.9, Opus-4.7 42.6) still fail on hard SAT/UNSAT items without tools; the plateau is not gone.

claim: Selection, not generation, is the test-time bottleneck on constraint puzzles: GPT-4o best-of-N with an oracle picker 60.3 (N=32) and 69.1 (N=128) vs majority vote 38.0 and reward-model best-of-N 34.8, greedy 31.7. A solver or checker can serve as the oracle where one exists.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare majority vote over N samples with N samples filtered by a code checker.
note_gap_search: Re-read (d09): no code checker was used in any best-of-N row; the oracle is the gold answer. Gap 6 open. Still single-source.

claim: A right label often comes with a wrong reasoning trace: SATBench trace accuracy is below prediction accuracy (o4-mini SAT 94.7 vs 74.6; Claude-3.7 SAT 83.2 vs 47.4); LINC reports CoT conclusions that differ from its own reasoning.
schema_part: G (verify, do not trust the trace)
agent_test: Grade final answers and a checked witness (assignment) separately; require a witness the code can check.

claim: Hidden reasoning tokens in o1-class models track the Z3 conflict count (about 400 tokens per conflict below 20 conflicts, plateau above 30), and wrong answers use more tokens than right ones.
agent_test: Use Z3 conflict count as a difficulty predictor to set the token budget before solving.
note_gap_search: Re-confirmed in ZebraLogic section 6.1 (d10): o1-mini 5,144.6 and o1-preview 5,346.3 mean hidden tokens vs 502.9 and 543.7 for GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o. Still one paper.

claim: A neural net trained on only the sat/unsat bit learns to find assignments (NeuroSAT: 85% accuracy on SR(40); 96% on unsat, 73% on sat; assignment decoded for 70% of satisfiable; 25% at SR(200) with 4x iterations) but is not competitive with real solvers.
agent_test: Not an agent test. Do not replace the solver with a learned guesser.

claim: An LLM proposing candidates that a sound SMT-based verifier checks beats the verifier alone on hard verification tasks: Lemur(GPT-4) solved 107 of 133 Code2Inv vs ESBMC 68, and 25 of 47 SV-COMP vs 1.
agent_test: Same pattern for our agent: LLM proposes, code verifies. Count proposals per solved item (Lemur averaged 4.7 to 8.6).

claim: Z3 as the search engine for combinatorial planning gives very large gains: TravelPlanner final pass 93.9% (test, Claude-3) vs 4.4% GPT-4 direct, no-solver ablation 25.2%; zero-shot optimal rates 72-100% vs 0-4% for a two-stage LLM planner on four other tasks.
agent_test: Use a hard-constraint planning task; compare LLM planner with and without a solver step at equal tokens.

claim: Fixed formal pipelines fail on fuzzy or commonsense questions: Proof of Thought on StrategyQA compiled 82.4% of programs but had precision 58.22% and false-positive rate 53.98%; Faithful CoT falls far below baselines on StrategyQA.
schema_part: G (when not to use the solver)
agent_test: Gate: use the solver path only when the task has crisp constraints; route fuzzy items to plain reasoning.
note_gap_search: Proof of Thought re-opened (d14): 82.4% compiled, precision 58.22%, FPR 53.98%. He and Wang (d08) add GPT-4o EntailmentBank CoT 81.8 vs Prolog zero-shot 27.4. Second independent source, so established.

claim: A sound solver is only sound for the formula, not for the problem: when translation drops unstated facts the pipeline is precise but incomplete (LINC GPT-4 predicts Uncertain 57% vs CoT 41%), and FOLIO's own screen found 39.2% of stories needed rewriting.
agent_test: After solving, have a second pass list implicit premises the spec lacks; count how often added premises change the answer.

claim: Writing the constraint model in a Python framework works better than in MiniZinc for current LLMs (DCP-Bench-Open: up to 75% vs 57.3% zero-shot; up to 91% with prompting and inference-time compute including self-verification).
agent_test: Prefer Z3Py or CPMpy over a separate modelling language in the agent's tool.

claim: Declarative output is not always easier to write: token log-likelihood favours the SAT form on GSM-Sys and CLUTRR but the PAL form on plain GSM; SatLM equals ProgLM on plain GSM.
agent_test: Choose declarative vs imperative per task type from a held-out pilot.

claim: When a CoT solver fails where Z3 succeeds, most errors are planning errors on constraint tasks (GSM-Sys 72.5%, CLUTRR 47.5%, GSM 42.5%), which a real solver removes; on plain GSM execution errors dominate (57.5%).
agent_test: Sample the agent's own failures; label planning vs execution errors; route planning-heavy classes to the solver.

claim: Self-consistency adds on top of the solver pipeline (SatLM GSM-Sys 69.4 to 80.9, GSM 71.8 to 84.8) while the logic gains remain mostly from the solver itself.
agent_test: Combine solver with 5-way voting; check marginal gain per extra token.

claim: Fine-tuning a small model to imitate solver reasoning removes parse failure as a dead end (LoGiPT 13B ProofWriter 81.17 vs Logic-LM GPT-4 79.66), but we do not train.
agent_test: Not testable without training; note only.

claim: LLMs can also test solvers: Fuzz4All generated SMT2 inputs and found bugs in Z3 and CVC5 (98 bugs over 9 systems, 64 confirmed new), so the solver is itself not infallible.
agent_test: Plug the returned model back into the original constraints as a cheap cross-check.

claim: Checking each CoT step by translating it to SMT-LIB gives a checkable audit of reasoning (VeriCoT: average 46% relative gain in verification pass rate with self-reflection), but the extracted result tables were unclear.
agent_test: Step-level checking of a small sample of traces vs end-answer checking, at equal tokens.

claim: Current frontier models (2026) still gain from a Python sandbox with SAT/SMT libraries on hard combinatorial SAT/UNSAT items: MathConstraint (329 items) mean +28 pp over 12 models; GPT-5.5 66.9 to 80.9, Claude-Opus-4.7 42.6 to 77.5, Gemini-3.1-Pro 51.7 to 72.9, Claude-4.6-Sonnet (no thinking budget) 18.5 to 70.5. Gain is smaller the more the model already thinks.
agent_test: Run the same 30 hard SAT items with thinking only and with a code sandbox at matched total tokens.

claim: Tool use can cost about the same tokens or less than long thinking for strong thinkers: GPT-5.5 10,880 tokens ($0.282) without tools vs 12,081 ($0.151) with; Opus-4.7 18,170 ($0.425) vs 23,441 ($0.208). For smaller or non-thinking models tokens rise (Gemini-3.1-Pro 5,420 vs 23,181; Sonnet 35,046 with tools). No equal-budget curve exists yet.
agent_test: Plot accuracy against total tokens for thinking-only vs spec-then-solve on one item set; report cost per correct answer.

claim: Solver-tool accuracy is budget-sensitive: success mostly needs several write-run-debug rounds. Halving 8 to 4 rounds costs up to 37 pp; SIM@1 is 0 to 20% for all models, SIM@8 36 to 81%. Plan for about 4 to 8 rounds and a fall-back answer when the budget ends.
agent_test: Cap solver rounds at 4 and 8 and compare accuracy; test force-submit rescue.

claim: A witness the code can verify exposes SAT-bias but does not remove it: without tools the gap between SAT-claim accuracy and verified accuracy is 12 to 54 pp (Sonnet +53.5, Llama +54.4, GPT-5.5 +12.1); with tools it is still 13 to 21 pp for GPT-5.5 and Sonnet. SATBench finds SAT-bias is 68.7% of o4-mini errors and 40.5% of R1 errors; an error-aware prompt fixed 60.4% and 73.2% of failing cases.
schema_part: G (never assert SAT without a checked witness)
agent_test: Require an assignment in the answer, check it by code, count how often a SAT claim fails the check.

claim: Solver wall time or conflict count does not tell which individual items LLMs fail once the set is already hard: within MathConstraint-hard, log solver time vs model accuracy r = -0.15 (no tools) and -0.14 (tools). It does separate easy from hard sets (median 0.20 s vs 2.52 s). The ZebraLogic link between Z3 conflicts and hidden tokens (K13) is about token use, not correctness.
agent_test: Test whether first-attempt verifier failure predicts needing more budget better than solver time.

claim: Which language the model writes is open. With a free choice, models often avoid Z3: Grok uses z3 in 44% of calls, Claude Sonnet and Opus use brute-force loops in 60% and 54%. GPT-4o on ZebraLogic does better in Python than Prolog (declarative one-shot avg 71.7 vs 58.8; zero-shot 38.1 vs 28.9), and Prolog has more syntax errors. No Z3Py vs CPMpy vs MiniZinc comparison exists.
agent_test: Give the same 20 puzzles to the agent with Z3Py, CP-SAT and brute force and record executable rate and correctness.

claim: Wrong routing is costly in both directions: a hard grid answered by CoT loses 50+ points vs Python (GPT-4o hard 8.9 vs 62.1), and a fuzzy entailment set sent to Prolog loses 54 points vs CoT (81.8 vs 27.4). Compile success is not a gate: Proof of Thought compiled 82.4% of StrategyQA programs with 58.22% precision. No measured gate classifier exists.
agent_test: Build a 3-question crispness check and test on 20 mixed items against always-solver and always-think.

claim: Silent wrong formalisation is acknowledged but unmeasured for model-written specs. VeriCoT states it cannot guarantee the translation is right; SATBench humans found 97% of its clause translations faithful (formula to text direction). No study compares round trip, second translation, or voting as detectors.
agent_test: Seed 20 problems with a dropped constraint and measure which check (round trip, second translation, model plug-in) catches it.
